name: Spring Nov release
tile_line: 90 advisories, mostly opt-in. Free fixes only on Boot 4.
tldr: Spring published 90 advisories on 19 Nov 2026. None has a public exploit or attacks, and most need an opt-in feature. On Boot 4, upgrade to the newest 4.x; Boot 3.5 and older get fixes only with paid support, so check which bugs apply.
summary: The advisories span Boot, Framework, Security, Spring AI, Integration, Web Services, Cloud and more.

affected.label: Spring Boot 4.1.2 or older
affected.text: Almost every advisory affects Spring Boot 4.1.2, 4.0.9 and older, or the Spring libraries those versions bring in (Framework, Security, Data, Integration, Web Services, LDAP). Spring AI and Spring Cloud have their own version numbers: see each bug. Spring Boot 4.2.0 came out the same day; the advisories don't list it either way. Check what your build actually resolves; with Gradle, run `./gradlew dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath` instead.

affected.label: You use an affected feature
affected.text: Each bug needs a specific feature or setup, listed under The bugs above. Most are opt-in: Spring AI vector stores and caches, Integration adapters, Cloud Gateway caching, RSocket. The widest reach: Spring Web Services endpoints (every one is exposed to oversized messages), Spring Boot apps with Actuator on Cloud Foundry, and Framework data binding with field exclusion rules.

do.label: On Boot 4: go to 4.1.3 or 4.0.10
do.text: These bring in the fixed Spring Security (7.1.3 / 7.0.9), Framework (7.0.11), Data, Integration (7.1.3 / 7.0.8) and Web Services (5.0.4) versions. Spring AI and Spring Cloud aren't managed by Boot: move to Spring AI 2.0.3, Cloud Gateway 5.0.5, Cloud Config 5.0.7 and Cloud Netflix 5.0.4 separately.

do.label: On Boot 3 or older: no free fix
do.text: Spring's fixes for Boot 3.5, 3.4 and 2.7 (3.5.18, 3.4.19, 2.7.36), Framework 6.x and 5.x, Security 6.x and 5.x, and Spring AI 1.x are only available with Enterprise support. Your options: move to Boot 4, buy Enterprise support, or use the workarounds for the bugs that affect you.

do.label: Check the critical ones first
do.text: [Spring Boot configured paths ending in /](/spring-boot-slash/) has a full page with checks. Spring Boot on Cloud Foundry: define your own security configuration. Spring AI Redis semantic cache: don't share the cache advisor across users. The LDAP one only affects test servers.

do.label: Workarounds if you can't upgrade
do.text: Spring Web Services: cap the request body size at your proxy or servlet container. Data Elasticsearch: reject query arguments containing `#{`. Cloud Config: take credentials out of the Git or SVN URL. Integration Redis queues: switch to a String or JSON serializer. Other bugs list theirs under The bugs above.

bugs.title: Redis semantic cache shares answers across users
bugs.text: Apps using `spring-ai-redis-semantic-cache` with a `SemanticCacheAdvisor` shared by several users can serve one user's cached answers to another, and an attacker can plant answers. The fix needs a code change (a `SemanticCacheScopeResolver`). Workaround: don't use the advisor in multi-user apps.

bugs.title: Cloud Foundry turns off default security
bugs.text: Servlet apps with Actuator deployed to Cloud Foundry lose Spring Boot's default web security. Reactive apps and apps with their own security configuration aren't affected. Workaround: define your own security configuration. Boot 3.5.0 to 4.1.2.

bugs.title: A configured path ending in / can skip security rules
bugs.text: Only if you set an Actuator or H2 console path that ends in a slash (for example `management.endpoints.web.path-mapping.health=status/`) or use `/` as the Actuator base path, and a later rule in your security config is looser. The fix only changes how configured paths become rules. Free fix only in 4.0.10 and 4.1.3.

bugs.title: ELRequestMatcher runs attacker-supplied code
bugs.text: Only if the app binds outside input onto a `RequestMatcher` property, a conversion meant for XML bean definitions, not user input. Spring lowered it to medium on 23 Nov: the attacker needs high privileges. Free fix only in 7.0.9 and 7.1.3.

bugs.title: Embedded test LDAP server is open to the network
bugs.text: The `spring-ldap-test` embedded server listens on every interface with a fixed, publicly known admin password. It matters only where tests run on a host others can reach (shared CI, a published container port), and only the throwaway test directory is exposed.

bugs.title: Coherence vector store filters can be bypassed
bugs.text: Apps on `CoherenceVectorStore` that pass user- or model-influenced filters can expose documents from other tenants.

bugs.title: Redis vector store filters can be bypassed
bugs.text: Apps on `RedisVectorStore` that put user values into filters can return other tenants' documents.

bugs.title: Typesense filters can be bypassed
bugs.text: Apps on `TypesenseVectorStore` that put untrusted values into filters can expose other tenants' documents.

bugs.title: Typesense grouped filters are mistranslated
bugs.text: Apps that rely on grouped (bracketed) Typesense filters for tenant or access rules may expose documents they shouldn't.

bugs.title: Config Server leaks Git and SVN passwords
bugs.text: If the repository URL contains `user:pass@`, every config response includes it in clear text. Workaround: use the separate username and password properties, or SSH keys.

bugs.title: Response cache keeps private responses
bugs.text: `LocalResponseCache` stores responses marked `private` or `no-store` when Cache-Control has more than one directive, as Spring Security's default does.

bugs.title: Eureka dashboard shows peer passwords
bugs.text: Eureka Server with the dashboard on (the default), credentials in the peer URLs, and the dashboard reachable without login.

bugs.title: Query arguments are run as code
bugs.text: Apps that pass untrusted input to a repository method with a string `@Query` and positional placeholders. Spring's score says the attacker needs a login; its text says a remote attacker. Workaround: reject input containing `#{`, or build queries with `CriteriaQuery` or `NativeQuery`.

bugs.title: Data binding can write fields you excluded
bugs.text: Only apps that keep nested, map or list fields out of binding with an exact `disallowedFields` (or restrictive `allowedFields`) pattern. Binding without such rules isn't described as affected. Free fix only in 7.0.11.

bugs.title: FTP chmod lets messages inject commands
bugs.text: Apps whose FTP adapter has the `chmod` option set and whose file names come from untrusted messages. No login needed.

bugs.title: Redis queues deserialize untrusted data
bugs.text: Redis queue endpoints use Java serialization by default, so anyone who can write to that Redis list can run code if a usable gadget class is present. Workaround: switch to a String or JSON serializer.

bugs.title: IP rules mix up IPv4 and IPv6
bugs.text: Apps that allow or block by IP (`hasIpAddress()` and similar) where the server can see IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses, for example on a dual-stack listener or behind a proxy that translates between the two. 7.1 only.

bugs.title: Oversized messages exhaust memory
bugs.text: Every Spring Web Services endpoint, no login and no special setup needed. The fix adds a 10 MB default limit. Workaround: cap the request body size at your proxy or servlet container.

bugs.title: Huge documents exhaust memory
bugs.text: Apps that read untrusted documents (uploads, URLs) with `TikaDocumentReader`. No login needed.

bugs.title: Nested filter expressions crash threads
bugs.text: Apps that accept filter expressions from users, for example in RAG search.

bugs.title: Crafted documents crash threads
bugs.text: Apps that read untrusted documents with the Tika or PDF readers.

bugs.title: Typesense delete can remove the wrong documents
bugs.text: Apps that pass user-supplied IDs to `delete()` on a Typesense store.

bugs.title: Actuator health path skips login on Jersey
bugs.text: Jersey apps (not Spring MVC or WebFlux) with Actuator and default Spring Security, where an authenticated JAX-RS resource shares a path with the health endpoint. Spring expects this to be rare.

bugs.title: JsonToGrpc filter leaks connections
bugs.text: Routes using the `JsonToGrpc` filter; repeated requests exhaust resources. No login needed.

bugs.title: Global response cache mixes up routes
bugs.text: The global `LocalResponseCache` with two routes on the same URI that differ by host, header or similar. Workaround: use the route-level cache instead.

bugs.title: MGET can write files outside the target folder
bugs.text: Apps using `MGET` on an FTP, SFTP or SMB gateway with `#remoteDirectory` in the local directory expression, connected to a hostile server.

bugs.title: JdbcMessageStore accepts any class
bugs.text: Apps that set allowed patterns on a `JdbcMessageStore` bean. An attacker who can already write to the message table can make the app deserialize any class.

bugs.title: WebAuthn doesn't catch cloned passkeys
bugs.text: The signature-counter check that detects a cloned authenticator doesn't work. The attacker must already have a copy of the victim's authenticator; Spring calls the check defense in depth.

bugs.title: RSocket basic auth can exhaust memory
bugs.text: Apps using RSocket security with the basic-auth payload converter, for example the deprecated `RSocketSecurity#basicAuthentication`. No login needed.

changes.text: CVE-2026-59273 (ELRequestMatcher) is now medium: Spring lowered it on 23 Nov. Four critical advisories remain.
